skill.name: find-bugs
skill.description: Guides AI assistants through a structured review of current branch changes to find bugs, vulnerabilities, and code quality issues.
skill.summary: Review branch changes for security issues, bugs, and quality defects.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a Markdown inline command example for git diff, not executable Ruby or shell backtick code. I found no prompt injection text or malicious intent in SKILL.md, and no semantic findings are added.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Get the FULL diff: `git diff master...HEAD`

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 contains a Markdown code span showing a fixed read-only git diff command. It is not Ruby backtick execution and has no user-controlled command injection path.

content.value_statement: Branch changes can hide security flaws, regressions, and missing verification. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused review workflow.
actual_capabilities: Reviews branch diffs for bugs, security vulnerabilities, and quality issues.
Maps user inputs, database queries, authorization checks, sessions, external calls, and cryptography.
Applies a security checklist covering injection, XSS, CSRF, races, sessions, disclosure, and denial of service.
Verifies potential issues against surrounding code and existing tests before reporting.
Formats findings with severity, evidence, fixes, and references.
limitations: Requires access to the branch diff and relevant changed files.
Does not modify code or apply fixes.
May miss issues outside the reviewed branch changes.
Depends on the assistant reading complete context when diffs are large.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge security review
use_cases.description: Review a feature branch before merge to find security issues and regressions.

use_cases.title: Release risk check
use_cases.description: Audit late-cycle changes for high-impact bugs before a deployment.

use_cases.title: Focused pull request audit
use_cases.description: Get a structured issue report that separates verified findings from uncertain areas.

prompt_templates.title: Basic branch review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a current branch review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current branch for bugs and security issues. Use the find-bugs workflow and report only verified findings.

prompt_templates.title: Security checklist review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this branch with the full security checklist. Map inputs, authorization, database access, sessions, external calls, and cryptography.

prompt_templates.title: Release readiness audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the branch for release-blocking defects. Prioritize critical and high severity issues, then list any areas that need manual verification.

prompt_templates.title: Deep verification pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a deep bug-finding pass on the branch. Read changed files completely, verify each finding, and include concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: Review my branch before I open a pull request.
output: One medium issue found in a changed authorization path.
The report explains the affected file and line, why the issue is real, and a concrete fix.

output_examples.input: Check this release branch for serious security problems.
output: No critical or high severity issues found.
The response lists reviewed files, completed checklist areas, and verification limits.
Two low-risk test coverage gaps are noted for follow-up.

best_practices: Run the skill after tests pass so findings can focus on real review risk.
Provide the full branch context when diffs are large or truncated.
Ask for severity and evidence when using the report for release decisions.
anti_patterns: Using the skill as a replacement for human security review on high-risk changes.
Reviewing only a truncated diff when changed files need full context.
Treating speculative findings as confirmed without checking the cited code.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It reports findings and suggested fixes, but it does not edit files.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What kind of issues does it prioritize?
faq.answer: It prioritizes security vulnerabilities, then functional bugs, then code quality issues.

faq.question: Can it review a partial diff?
faq.answer: It can start from a partial diff, but the workflow asks the assistant to read complete changed files.

faq.question: Does it include references?
faq.answer: Yes. The output format asks for relevant standards or references when applicable.

faq.question: What happens if no issues are found?
faq.answer: The skill instructs the assistant to say that clearly and avoid inventing findings.
